live.name: ALPHV
live.headline: ALPHV: a ransomware actor known by several names
live.in_short: The catalogue lists ALPHV under several aliases and a set of tools. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: ALPHV is the main name for this actor in the catalogue record.
It is also listed as ALPHVM, Ambitious Scorpius, BlackCat Gang and UNC4466.
The catalogue links the name to tools including BlackCat, Noberus, Munchkin, Mimikatz, Impacket, PsExec, LaZagne, MEGAsync and GO Simple Tunnel (GOST).
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.name: ALPHV
next.headline: ALPHV (BlackCat): a Rust-based ransomware-as-a-service gang known for leak-site extortion and a 2024 exit scam
next.in_short: ALPHV, also called BlackCat, ran a ransomware-as-a-service operation from November 2021. It stole data, pressed victims on a leak site, drew a 2023 FBI disruption, and in March 2024 appeared to run an exit scam.

sentences.t: ALPHV is also known as ALPHVM, BlackCat, Noberus, Ambitious Scorpius and UNC4466.
Malpedia says ALPHV has been seen in ransomware attacks since November 18, 2021.
Malpedia describes it as a Rust ransomware family sold as ransomware-as-a-service. It runs on Windows, Linux and VMware ESXi.
BleepingComputer reports that ALPHV is believed to be a rebrand of the DarkSide and BlackMatter operations.

Cisco Talos says the links between BlackMatter and BlackCat are probable. It has moderate confidence that BlackMatter affiliates were among BlackCat's early adopters. A BlackCat representative said the two groups were connected but that BlackCat was not a rebrand.
Sygnia attributed one 2023 intrusion to BlackCat (ALPHV) or one of its affiliates, not to a single confirmed actor.
The group has hit a wide mix of victims. Reports name a county government, a Canadian software group, a dental and medical distributor, an Indian drug maker and a mortgage lender.
Recorded Future News says the group has made a point of going after healthcare and pharmaceutical companies.
The FBI linked the gang to over 60 breaches in its first four months, from November 2021 to March 2022, according to BleepingComputer.
Malpedia says the ransomware can encrypt files with AES or ChaCha20. It can delete volume shadow copies and stop services and ESXi virtual machines. It can spread to other hosts using PsExec.

Symantec reported updates in 2022 that added an ARM build, safe-mode encryption and searchable leak sites. It also saw an updated Exmatter exfiltration tool, and an affiliate using the Eamfo infostealer against Veeam backup credentials.

In one Sygnia case, access came through a compromised third-party vendor. The attacker spent weeks moving through the network with Cobalt Strike and tunnelling tools. It copied data to cloud storage with Rclone and then sent extortion emails.
The eSentire Threat Response Unit reported Russian-speaking affiliates using Google ads to lure users into downloading the Nitrogen initial-access malware, which led to ALPHV/BlackCat ransomware.
Victims were pressed through a leak site. In the Constellation Software case, the gang claimed to have stolen over 1 TB and leaked some documents as proof.
In September 2022, DataBreaches reported that BlackCat claimed the Suffolk County attack, which disabled the county's 911 system. The group claimed 400 GB of data.

In a statement relayed by one article, AlphV said it launched ransomware against more than 100 ESXi hypervisors at MGM Resorts on September 11, 2023. The article treats all of these claims as AlphV's own and unverified.
Henry Schein disclosed an incident on October 15. The report says AlphV claimed responsibility and re-encrypted systems after negotiations broke down.

BleepingComputer reports that the FBI disrupted the gang in December 2023 and temporarily took down its Tor negotiation and leak sites. It says the FBI estimated at least $300 million in ransom payments from over 1,000 victims until September 2023.

In February 2024, unnamed sources told BleepingComputer the Change Healthcare attack was linked to BlackCat. The site could not confirm this. UnitedHealth's SEC filing described a suspected nation-state actor.

In March 2024, BleepingComputer judged that the gang appeared to be running an exit scam. Its sites went offline, affiliates said they were not paid, and a fake FBI seizure banner appeared. Europol and the NCA said they were not involved.
A December 2025 Justice Department release, listed on Malpedia, says two Americans pleaded guilty to targeting US victims with ALPHV BlackCat ransomware.
Keep offline backups and protect backup credentials, since reports describe attackers going after backup tools.
Check third-party vendor access and virtual host security, because both appear in the cases above.
